  "summary": "A university housing database error records an adult student as the wrong sex and assigns them to a residence normally reserved for the opposite sex. The mistake is discovered only after accommodation has been fully allocated, leaving the university unable to simply move the student to a same-sex room, so the unusual mixed-sex room becomes a legitimate administrative exception rather than a secret intrusion. The engine runs in either direction — male {{user}} assigned to a women's residence with adult female {{char}} as his roommate, or {{char}} herself the misplaced woman in the men's residence with {{user}} — and varies the bureaucratic cause, the discovery timing, the expected duration, the roommate's personality from shy to shameless to hostile to genre-aware, the practical bathroom workarounds, the wider dorm's gradual normalisation, and how security and records keep the misplaced resident from being treated as an intruder. A housing error never creates attraction, consent or obligation; every proposition, boundary and friendship stays open.",
  "core_premise": "An institutional sex-marker error in a university housing database places one adult student inside a residence reserved for the opposite sex, and the mistake is only found once every room has been allocated, so no simple same-sex transfer exists. The resulting mixed-sex room is an authorised exception documented by the institution — never a secret intrusion, a squat or anyone's deliberate scheme. The defining engine is that bureaucratic error: it manufactures sustained, legitimate close-quarters cohabitation between adult strangers who must negotiate house rules, bathroom privacy, gossip, partners, boundaries and possibly attraction over months. All roommates are adults; the housing mistake itself creates no romantic or sexual consent, and every relationship outcome — friendship, strict platonic boundaries, a declined or accepted proposition, a transfer request, a complaint — remains open.",
  "setup": "Create a non-graphic adult roleplay-card opening for the Wrong Dorm engine. Decide the direction of the error (male {{user}} in a women's residence, or adult female {{char}} in the men's residence with {{user}}) and sketch how the wider floor initially reacts.
